question: Which of these is a classic example of environmental asphyxia?

options.A: Severe diabetic ketoacidosis
options.B: An acute myocardial infarction
options.C: Drowning in a swimming pool
options.D: A sudden allergic asthma attack

explanation: Environmental asphyxia happens when outside factors—like water, smoke, or a tight space—keep a person from reaching clean air. Water in a pool is a clear external block! [learn more](GNS112_U7_T1#GNS112_U7_T1_h2)

question: What is the final outcome of spermatogenesis in human males?

options.A: One large ovum and three polar bodies
options.B: Two identical diploid zygotes
options.C: Four functional spermatozoa
options.D: One functional sperm and three polar bodies

explanation: Great job! Unlike egg formation which makes just one large egg, spermatogenesis neatly divides to produce four healthy, ready-to-go sperm cells. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T3#GNS121_U6_T3_h1)

question: What is a major ethical dilemma an occupational health nurse frequently faces?

options.A: Deciding whether to do surgery without a doctor
options.B: Balancing loyalty to the employer with the duty to protect worker health and privacy
options.C: Choosing between clinical nursing and selling products
options.D: Reporting fellow nurses to criminal courts for minor errors

explanation: Spot on! Because the company pays your salary but nursing ethics demand patient privacy, it can be a tough tightrope to walk. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h8)

question: Through which route does a pathogen typically leave a human body?

options.A: Intact and healthy skin layers
options.B: Respiratory secretions or body fluids
options.C: Nutritional supplements in the diet
options.D: White blood cells in the bone marrow

explanation: Spot on! Pathogens love to hitch a ride out of the body through fluids, mucus, cough droplets, or open skin sores. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T1#GNS313_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the main job of the chairperson during a professional meeting?

options.A: Serving refreshments to all invited attendees
options.B: Guiding discussion and keeping the team on the agenda
options.C: Taking over patient care duties while staff are away
options.D: Writing down every single word spoken by participants

explanation: The chairperson leads the session, manages time, and ensures the group sticks to the planned topics. [learn more](GST321_U7_T4#GST321_U7_T4_h4)

question: What is the main difference between 'perfect use' and 'typical use' of a contraceptive method?

options.A: Typical use accounts for human error and real-life inconsistencies
options.B: Typical use always has a higher success rate than perfect use
options.C: Perfect use is calculated only in elderly clients
options.D: Perfect use includes the cost of purchasing the supply items

explanation: Perfect use assumes the method is used flawlessly every single time, while typical use reflects real human life—like missing a pill or a barrier breaking. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T5#GNS225_U3_T5_h5)

question: Why are strong opioid painkillers usually avoided for routine home care after an abortion?

options.A: They carry high risks of sedation, nausea, and dependency
options.B: They permanently damage the lining of the stomach
options.C: They cause the uterus to stop contracting completely
options.D: They raise blood pressure to dangerously high levels

explanation: Routine cramps can usually be handled safely with milder drugs, sparing the patient from heavy side effects like sleepiness and nausea. Makes total sense! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h3)

question: What is the main difference between endocrine and exocrine glands?

options.A: Endocrine glands lack ducts and release hormones directly into the blood
options.B: Exocrine glands possess a rich network of fenestrated capillaries
options.C: Endocrine glands secrete substances exclusively onto the skin surface
options.D: Exocrine glands produce chemical messengers while endocrine glands do not

explanation: Think of endocrine glands as ductless delivery systems! Because they don't have tubes (ducts), they dump their hormones straight into the bloodstream to travel round the body. You've got this! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T2#GNS211_U1_T2_h1)

question: During body development before birth, the labia majora grow from the exact same tissue that forms which male structure?

options.A: The vas deferens
options.B: The seminal vesicles
options.C: The scrotum
options.D: The prostate gland

explanation: Fascinating, right? Embryology shows us how different structures develop from the same root tissues. The labia majora correspond to the male scrotum! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T1#GNS121_U5_T1_h2)

question: A patient with severe fatigue insists on cleaning their whole house in one go, leaving them bedridden for days afterward. What nursing advice should you give?

options.A: Avoid all movement for the next month to let muscles heal.
options.B: Break chores into small parts and rest between each task.
options.C: Increase caffeine intake to maintain speed through the cleaning.
options.D: Perform all cleaning tasks immediately after waking up.

explanation: You're learning great clinical judgment! Splitting big tasks into smaller chunks and resting in between helps patients break the exhausting 'boom-and-bust' cycle. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T3#GNS123_U3_T3_h6)

question: What communication style should a nurse use when counseling a caregiver who defaulted on vaccines?

options.A: Total silence while the caregiver reads a pamphlet
options.B: Rapid medical terminology to prove professional status
options.C: Strict lecturing to show authority and clinical power
options.D: Respectful listening and clear, non-judgmental explanations

explanation: Caregivers respond better to patience and empathy than to strict scolding, which often makes them avoid the clinic permanently. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h5)

question: What are the two main parts of the human immune system?

options.A: Primary and secondary defense
options.B: Innate and adaptive immunity
options.C: Cellular and humoral barriers
options.D: Active and passive antibodies

explanation: Great job! The immune system has two main teams: innate immunity (the fast, born-with-it guards) and adaptive immunity (the smart specialists that learn to fight specific germs over time). You've got this! [learn more](GNS123_U4_T2#GNS123_U4_T2_h1)

question: What makes a Type B drug reaction so tricky compared to other reactions?

options.A: It can always be calculated using the patient's exact weight
options.B: It disappears completely if the patient drinks more water
options.C: It happens suddenly and does not depend on the dose
options.D: It only occurs when the drug expires on the shelf

explanation: Type B reactions are bizarre and unexpected. They can happen out of nowhere, no matter if the dose is tiny or large! [learn more](GNS215_U2_T5#GNS215_U2_T5_h2)

question: What is the primary medical goal when admitting a patient with hyperemesis gravidarum?

options.A: Feeding the patient a heavy high-protein meal right away
options.B: Starting immediate surgical options to empty the uterus
options.C: Discharging the patient with herbal teas and rest
options.D: Correcting fluid and electrolyte imbalances with IV fluids

explanation: Before anything else, we must rehydrate and restore lost electrolytes to keep vital organs safe. You're thinking like a real ward nurse! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h6)

question: What does 'vicarious liability' mean for you as a nurse?

options.A: A nurse carrying personal professional indemnity insurance
options.B: An employer being held responsible for an employee's mistake
options.C: A patient taking legal action directly against the state government
options.D: A doctor supervising medical students during clinical rounds

explanation: Vicarious liability simply means the hospital or your employer can share the blame if you make a mistake while doing your normal job duties. You're not always standing alone! [learn more](GST321_U10_T6#GST321_U10_T6_h1)

question: What does 'inter-rater reliability' check for in clinical exams?

options.A: Whether students take the same test twice without cheating
options.B: Whether different evaluators give similar scores for the same performance
options.C: How well the exam predicts future success on the job
options.D: If the test measures what it was originally designed to measure

explanation: It checks if two different lecturers would give you the same score for the identical performance. Fairness is key! [learn more](GST321_U9_T1#GST321_U9_T1_h5)

question: What is the main difference between medical asepsis (clean technique) and surgical asepsis (sterile technique)?

options.A: Surgical asepsis relies entirely on chemical disinfectants rather than physical barriers
options.B: Surgical asepsis eliminates all microorganisms, while medical asepsis reduces their number and spread
options.C: Medical asepsis is used only in operating theatres, while surgical asepsis is for general wards
options.D: Medical asepsis destroys bacterial spores, whereas surgical asepsis only targets viruses

explanation: Well done! Clean technique (medical asepsis) cuts down germ numbers, while sterile technique (surgical asepsis) wipes out every single micro-organism. [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h4)

question: What is the primary focus of the DASH diet for managing high blood pressure?

options.A: Eating plenty of fruits, vegetables, and low-fat dairy while reducing sodium
options.B: Eliminating all carbohydrates completely from daily meals
options.C: Eating only raw meat and root vegetables
options.D: Drinking large amounts of herbal teas and liquid supplements

explanation: The DASH diet emphasizes nutrient-dense whole foods and mineral-rich produce while cutting back on salt and unhealthy fats. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T16#GNS324_U4_T16_h4)

question: Why is there a higher risk of developing gallstones during pregnancy?

options.A: The growing uterus crushes the bile duct and blocks fluid flow
options.B: The liver stops producing bile salts entirely during the first trimester
options.C: Bile stays in the gallbladder longer and becomes supersaturated with cholesterol
options.D: High iron supplements crystallize inside the biliary tree

explanation: When bile sits around too long and mixes with extra pregnancy cholesterol, it forms stones easily. Makes total sense when you think about it! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h5)

question: A village thinks their stream water is fine, but lab tests show it is full of harmful bacteria. The nurse steps in to treat the water. What kind of need is this?

options.A: Normative need
options.B: Expressed need
options.C: Comparative need
options.D: Felt need

explanation: Even though the villagers didn't complain, professional testing uncovered the hidden danger. That expert-defined standard makes it a normative need! [learn more](GNS124_U3_T2#GNS124_U3_T2_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of translating a community problem into a formal nursing diagnosis?

options.A: To replace all medical doctors in the primary healthcare center
options.B: To hide community health failures from government inspectors
options.C: To increase the cost of health services for local residents
options.D: To bridge data collection and structure a focused, goal-oriented care plan

explanation: A formal nursing diagnosis turns raw findings into a clear statement that guides planning and intervention. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h7)

question: What is a big benefit of using digital inventory systems instead of paper records?

options.A: It ensures clinical injections never cause skin pain
options.B: It completely stops nurses from ever needing to count items
options.C: It lets central managers view stock data across sites quickly
options.D: It stops medical supplies from reaching their expiration date

explanation: Spot on! Digital systems link different clinics together, making it super easy to spot trends and shortages early. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h5)

question: A community health nurse is talking to abattoir (slaughterhouse) workers about their daily risks. Which animal-borne diseases should be the main focus?

options.A: Cerebrospinal meningitis
options.B: Cholera and typhoid fever
options.C: Anthrax and brucellosis
options.D: Malaria and yellow fever

explanation: You nailed it! Because abattoir workers handle livestock directly, they are at higher risk for zoonotic infections like anthrax and brucellosis. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h2)

question: Why is the liver considered such a vital metabolic organ for the whole body?

options.A: It processes nutrients, filters toxins, and stores essential vitamins
options.B: It produces strong mechanical churning motions to break down fiber
options.C: It pumps oxygenated blood directly through the major heart valves
options.D: It absorbs all water from solid waste before elimination

explanation: The liver is like the body's ultimate multitasking chemical factory. It handles nutrients, cleans out toxins, and stores vitamins to keep everything running smoothly. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T5#GNS121_U1_T5_h3)

question: When a drainage tube gets blocked, which of these actions is completely WRONG and dangerous?

options.A: Pushing a partially dislodged tube back into the body cavity
options.B: Checking the entire length of the tubing for accidental kinks
options.C: Inspecting the tube for visible blood clots or mucus plugs
options.D: Notifying the medical team if output remains absent

explanation: You got it! Pushing a slipped tube back inside drags surface bacteria straight into sterile tissues. Always check with your senior or doctor first. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T22#GNS212_U1_T22_h6)

question: You are starting a new maternal health project in a rural village. What should be your very first step when designing its monitoring plan?

options.A: Purchase expensive computer servers for data storage
options.B: Discontinue all existing paper health registers immediately
options.C: Define the main goals and objectives of the health program
options.D: Hire international consultants to write the final evaluation report

explanation: You can't measure your progress until you clearly know what the project is trying to achieve first! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T21#GNS225_U2_T21_h4)

question: A public health nurse wants to quickly create awareness about a sudden cholera outbreak across an entire state. Which IEC channel is most appropriate?

options.A: Mass media like radio broadcasts and billboards
options.B: One-on-one counseling sessions inside the antenatal clinic
options.C: A single home visit to the village chief's residence
options.D: Written letters mailed to individual households

explanation: Mass media is the best choice when a large geographical population needs urgent awareness about an immediate health threat. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T2#GNS124_U5_T2_h5)

question: Which of the following conditions is a classic example of a metabolic crisis in diabetes?

options.A: Prolonged hypoglycemia
options.B: Diabetic ketoacidosis
options.C: Diabetic neuropathy
options.D: Chronic foot ulceration

explanation: Diabetic ketoacidosis is an acute, life-threatening metabolic emergency caused by severe insulin deficiency and acid buildup. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h7)

question: What is the main danger of having an extremely wide span of control on a busy ward?

options.A: Staff members will have too many layers of bosses to report to
options.B: Communication between departments will completely stop
options.C: Supervision can become stretched too thin, risking safety
options.D: Every nurse will be promoted to a management position

explanation: Spot on! If one nurse manager is trying to oversee too many staff at once, it's easy to miss mistakes and patient safety can suffer. [learn more](GST321_U1_T9#GST321_U1_T9_h5)

question: Which of the following is an appropriate nursing action when supporting a family undergoing genetic counseling?

options.A: Telling the family which genetic diagnosis they should accept
options.B: Making the final decision on whether the couple should have children
options.C: Ordering complex chromosomal laboratory tests independently
options.D: Reinforcing educational information and providing emotional support

explanation: Nurses support patients by reinforcing explanations given by genetic specialists and offering a compassionate listening ear, while respecting patient autonomy. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h7)

question: Why is it so helpful to offer contraceptives right inside the PAC clinic before the patient leaves?

options.A: It prevents nurses from having to talk about reproductive anatomy
options.B: It forces every client to accept an intrauterine device before leaving
options.C: It guarantees that the clinic receives extra financial donations
options.D: It removes the barrier of traveling elsewhere and ensures immediate protection

explanation: Providing birth control right on the spot ensures women leave fully protected before fertility returns, so they don't slip through the cracks of a separate referral. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a core responsibility of the community health nurse in a referral?

options.A: Writing a clear referral note detailing findings and treatments
options.B: Performing major complex surgeries at the primary clinic
options.C: Assessing the patient's condition to spot danger signs early
options.D: Conducting follow-up home visits after the patient returns

explanation: Primary health clinics do not have the facilities for major surgeries; such cases are referred upward. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h6)

question: What is the basic structural and functional unit of the human body?

options.A: A tissue
options.B: The molecule
options.C: The cell
options.D: An organ

explanation: The cell is universally recognized as the smallest independent unit that can carry out all life processes in the body. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why do patients with untreated diabetes always feel very thirsty and pee a lot?

options.A: Excess blood sugar pulls large amounts of water into the urine as the kidneys filter it out
options.B: Dehydration is caused by a simultaneous infection in the bladder
options.C: The liver stores extra water to dilute circulating blood sugar
options.D: High insulin levels trick the brain into thinking the body is dehydrated

explanation: When the kidneys try to wash away all that extra sugar, water naturally follows it out. That leads to heavy urination and leaves the patient feeling super thirsty. Makes total sense when you picture it! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h2)

question: When does monitoring of a community health program actually happen?

options.A: Before any assessment or planning begins
options.B: Only after the entire project has completely ended
options.C: Five years after everyone has forgotten the project
options.D: While the program is actively running

explanation: Great job! Monitoring is ongoing supervision that happens live during implementation so you can catch and fix mistakes right away. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h7)

question: Why should pregnant women with vulval varicosities try hard to avoid constipation?

options.A: Bowel pressure directly blocks the arterial supply to the labia
options.B: Straining during bowel movements increases pelvic venous pressure
options.C: Constipation stops the kidneys from filtering blood properly
options.D: Hard stools can physically puncture the dilated perineal veins

explanation: Straining pushes extra pressure downward into veins that are already stretched to their limit. Encouraging fluids and fiber helps keep things soft and protects those veins! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T9#GNS216_U5_T9_h5)

question: What is the primary target group for public or community-funded nurseries?

options.A: Children who have already graduated from primary school
options.B: Low-income families and vulnerable populations who need subsidized support
options.C: Exclusively infants who require long-term neonatal intensive care
options.D: Only high-earning corporate executives seeking elite private tutors

explanation: Public and community nurseries are usually subsidized by governments or NGOs to ensure affordable childcare access for families with limited resources. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h2)

question: How do antisecretory medications like racecadotril help manage diarrhoea?

options.A: They permanently paralyze the smooth muscles of the bowel
options.B: They reduce fluid and electrolyte secretion into the gut
options.C: They coat the entire stomach lining to block all acid
options.D: They kill all viruses present in the bloodstream

explanation: Instead of stopping gut movement, these drugs tell the intestines to stop pumping so much water and salt into your tummy. Clever, right? [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h5)

question: Which external structure is a small, highly sensitive erectile organ?

options.A: Labia majora
options.B: Mons pubis
options.C: Clitoris
options.D: Bartholin gland

explanation: The clitoris sits at the top of the labia minora and contains many nerve endings for sexual sensation. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the primary structural and functional unit of the human kidney?

options.A: The collecting duct
options.B: The nephron
options.C: The renal pelvis
options.D: The loop of Henle

explanation: The nephron is recognized as the basic working unit responsible for filtering blood and producing urine inside the kidney. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T5#GNS121_U2_T5_h1)

question: What is the immediate correct action if a surgical sponge count is incorrect at the end of a surgery?

options.A: Assume the package count was wrong at the factory and ignore it
options.B: Document the missing sponge in the chart and finish closing quickly
options.C: Stop closure immediately and search the wound and room until found
options.D: Order an x-ray for tomorrow morning after the patient wakes up

explanation: Never rush past a bad count! Closing must pause immediately so a full search can be done to ensure no item is left inside the patient. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T4#GNS123_U5_T4_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of patient education in diabetes management?

options.A: To ensure the patient memorizes complex medical terminology
options.B: To shift all responsibilities of treatment onto family members
options.C: To empower the patient to safely manage their daily care
options.D: To eliminate the need for any follow-up visits at the clinic

explanation: Since diabetes is a daily home-managed condition, education equips patients with the skills needed to make safe lifestyle and treatment decisions. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h7)

question: Why is the outer one-inch border of a sterile field considered unsterile?

options.A: Because nurses are only allowed to touch the exact center of the tray
options.B: Because air currents move faster along the edges of a paper wrap
options.C: Because the manufacturer marks that area with special invisible ink
options.D: Because it is likely to touch unsterile surfaces during setup and handling

explanation: Makes sense, right? That outer edge is bound to brush against your hands or the table surface while you open it, so we treat it as a safe buffer zone that's no longer sterile. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T2#GNS122_U2_T2_h3)

question: Why is HIV disclosure considered a complex process for many patients?

options.A: It often involves heavy emotional strain and fear of social stigma
options.B: It is illegal in most healthcare jurisdictions without a judge's order
options.C: It requires advanced surgical training to explain to partners
options.D: It permanently stops the transmission of all other viral infections

explanation: Fear of rejection, discrimination, and violence makes sharing an HIV-positive status very difficult for many individuals. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h1)

question: Why isn't just treating sick patients enough to stop a waterborne disease outbreak?

options.A: The environmental reservoir remains contaminated and causes reinfection
options.B: Waterborne pathogens cannot be killed by boiling
options.C: Antibiotics do not work against bacteria found in water
options.D: Patients always become asymptomatic carriers after recovery

explanation: If you don't fix the dirty water supply, people will keep drinking it and falling right back sick. You've got to fix the source! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h5)

question: If a Nigerian community suddenly sees an outbreak of measles, what is the most likely cause?

options.A: Low routine immunization coverage among children
options.B: High mosquito vector breeding during the rainy season
options.C: Unsafe disposal of hospital sharp instruments
options.D: Contaminated local drinking water supplies

explanation: Well done! Measles is totally preventable with vaccines, so sudden outbreaks usually mean kids in the area are missing their routine shots. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T96#GNS214_U1_T96_h2)

question: What is a crucial instruction for a patient who just had cryotherapy (freezing) for symptomatic cervical ectropion?

options.A: Increase strenuous physical exercise to speed up pelvic blood flow
options.B: Expect complete absence of vaginal discharge for at least two months
options.C: Avoid sexual intercourse and tampon use for a specified healing period
options.D: Perform vigorous vaginal douching twice daily to clear debris

explanation: Pelvic rest is vital after cryotherapy to give the treated cervical tissue time to heal safely without introducing infection. Excellent clinical advice to remember! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h6)

question: Why is encouraging increased fluid intake the most crucial home care instruction after a barium swallow?

options.A: To dilute any remaining stomach acid and prevent heartburn symptoms
options.B: To speed up the healing of small tears made during the X-ray
options.C: To prevent the barium from hardening and causing constipation or bowel blockage
options.D: To help the kidneys absorb the radioactive barium into the urine

explanation: Extra fluids keep the barium mixture moving smoothly through the colon, preventing it from turning into a concrete-like blockage. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a common feature of end-of-life care in Nigeria?

options.A: Involvement of extended family in medical discussions
options.B: Widespread legal use of formal living wills and advance directives
options.C: Strong influence of Christian and Islamic religious beliefs
options.D: Strict criminal prohibitions against assisted suicide and euthanasia

explanation: While family involvement, religion, and strict laws against euthanasia are very common in Nigeria, formal written living wills are still not widely used or legally integrated into everyday hospital practice yet. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T7#GNS321_U4_T7_h7)

question: In the chain of infection, what is the main job of an infective host?

options.A: To act exclusively as a dead-end for microbial life
options.B: To harbor an infectious agent and serve as a source of infection
options.C: To manufacture antibodies for community protection
options.D: To destroy invading pathogens before symptoms appear

explanation: You've got this! Think of the host as a comfortable home for the germ. It gives the pathogen a place to stay and acts as the starting point for spreading to others. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T3#GNS313_U1_T3_h1)

question: Which of these is a direct legal duty for a nurse administrator?

options.A: Setting national monetary tax policies
options.B: Importing foreign medical machinery
options.C: Maintaining safe staffing levels and proper equipment
options.D: Fixing electrical faults in the hospital building

explanation: Spot on! Nurse managers must legally protect patients and staff by making sure the unit has enough hands and working tools. [learn more](GST321_U10_T2#GST321_U10_T2_h4)

question: Why might a struggling family find it hard to follow advice about eating a balanced diet?

options.A: Local health nurses refuse to give them recipe books
options.B: Daily survival and food costs take priority over long-term health
options.C: Traditional beliefs forbid the eating of vegetables
options.D: They lack basic interest in learning about nutrition

explanation: When money is tight, finding food for today always comes before thinking about long-term wellness. Empathy is key here! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T27#GNS225_U2_T27_h5)

question: What is the main perk of doing a 24-hour urine collection instead of just one blood test?

options.A: It captures total hormone output and smooths out hourly spikes
options.B: It measures intracellular hormone synthesis inside the bone marrow
options.C: It requires no special patient preparation or storage rules
options.D: It can be completed in less than five minutes at the bedside

explanation: Hormones can spike and dip all day long. Collecting urine over a full 24 hours gives a complete, average picture of what the body is putting out! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T4#GNS222_U2_T4_h3)

question: What action should a nurse take immediately if a medication administration error occurs?

options.A: Ask the patient to keep quiet about the mistake
options.B: Hide the empty medicine cup in the trash can
options.C: Wait until the end of the month to see if harm happens
options.D: Report it to the doctor and nurse manager right away

explanation: Immediate reporting ensures the patient gets quick medical evaluation and treatment if an adverse effect develops. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h7)

question: Why must nurses condition ice packs before putting them in a daily vaccine carrier?

options.A: To prevent the accidental freezing of freeze-sensitive vaccines
options.B: To ensure the ice melts faster during the hot afternoon sun
options.C: To make the vaccine carrier lighter for the nurse to carry
options.D: To activate the chemical VVM label on the vaccine vials

explanation: Direct contact with rock-solid ice can freeze and ruin liquid vaccines like tetanus. Conditioning the ice keeps the temperature just right! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h2)

question: What is the first physical action a nurse should take when non-reassuring foetal heart patterns appear?

options.A: Change the mother's position to her side
options.B: Prepare the operating room for a caesarean section
options.C: Administer a strong dose of pain medication
options.D: Encourage the mother to push with all her strength

explanation: Turning the mother to her side takes pressure off major blood vessels, instantly improving blood return to the heart and placental blood flow. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h5)

question: What is a very common baby-related issue linked to maternal chronic kidney disease?

options.A: Excessive birth weight
options.B: Fetal bone overgrowth
options.C: Intrauterine growth restriction
options.D: Delayed closure of fontanelles

explanation: Because the placenta gets less nourishment, the baby's growth can slow down inside the womb, leading to low birth weight. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T007#GNS226_U4_T007_h3)

question: How does gender discrimination often show up inside everyday healthcare settings?

options.A: Via written notices refusing service to women
options.B: Through hidden biases in daily routines
options.C: By official hospital policy stating unequal care
options.D: Through mandatory fees for male patients

explanation: Institutional bias is usually subtle. It sneaks into everyday clinical routines and unspoken habits rather than being written down as an official rule. Great job thinking critically about this! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T22#GNS225_U5_T22_h1)

question: Which of these can act as a reservoir where germs live?

options.A: Completely dry and sunny metal surfaces
options.B: Sterile surgical instruments only
options.C: Soil, water, humans, and animals
options.D: Intact human skin with no normal flora

explanation: Germs aren't picky! They can live inside living hosts like humans and animals, or in the environment like soil and water. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T5#GNS313_U1_T5_h2)

question: What must an assisted living facility do after inspectors find a safety or rule violation during a visit?

options.A: Submit and implement a formal plan of correction
options.B: Immediately close the building and relocate all residents
options.C: Change the state laws to match current facility practices
options.D: Ignore the finding if staff members disagree with it

explanation: Spot on! When inspectors find a problem, the facility has to write down a clear plan showing how they will fix it and make sure it never happens again. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h7)

question: Where should you aim the stream of water inside the ear canal?

options.A: Straight down the bottom floor of the canal
options.B: Directly at the center of the eardrum
options.C: Against the center of the wax plug only
options.D: Against the top or back wall of the canal

explanation: Aiming along the canal wall lets the water slip behind the wax and push it out gently, without blasting the delicate eardrum. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T11#GNS122_U1_T11_h4)

question: A clinic logs 95 babies for Pentavalent 1, but only 60 return for Pentavalent 3. What does this show?

options.A: A successful outreach campaign with no service delivery gaps
options.B: An excellent level of continuous retention in the immunization clinic
options.C: A high program dropout rate requiring immediate community follow-up
options.D: An oversupply of vaccines that requires immediate redistribution

explanation: Dropping from 95 down to 60 means many infants aren't completing their schedule. Time for some community tracking and follow-up! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T75#GNS214_U1_T75_h5)

question: Which traditional method uses heat from the sun to remove moisture from crops?

options.A: Refrigeration
options.B: Sun-drying
options.C: Irradiation
options.D: Pasteurization

explanation: Sun-drying is a classic, natural method using solar heat and fresh air to dry out things like grains and peppers. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T011#GNS227_U3_T011_h3)

question: A nursing researcher states: 'To examine if handwashing frequency reduces hospital-acquired infections.' What is this statement?

options.A: A research objective
options.B: A data collection tool
options.C: A research hypothesis
options.D: A final study conclusion

explanation: Spotting an action verb like 'to examine' right at the beginning is a dead giveaway that you're looking at a research objective! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T9#GNS217_U3_T9_h3)

question: What is 'member checking' when doing qualitative research?

options.A: Sharing findings back with participants to confirm accuracy
options.B: Testing the audio recorder battery before an interview
options.C: Reviewing staff membership lists for the research team
options.D: Checking if participants paid their hospital bills

explanation: Brilliant! Member checking means going back to your participants to say, 'Did I get your story right?' It ensures your interpretation is honest and true. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h8)

question: Why is it important for a nurse manager to understand basic labour laws?

options.A: To calculate the exact profit margin of the hospital pharmacy
options.B: To replace the hospital human resource department entirely
options.C: To prevent illegal disciplinary actions and costly hospital lawsuits
options.D: To write medical prescriptions for patients in emergency wards

explanation: Knowing labour laws helps nurse managers treat staff fairly and legally, protecting both the workers' rights and the hospital from unnecessary court cases. [learn more](GST321_U4_T1#GST321_U4_T1_h7)

question: What actually drives water to move passively across the wall of the intestine?

options.A: Active water pumps on the enterocyte membrane
options.B: Changes in core body temperature
options.C: Direct muscle contractions of the villi
options.D: Osmotic gradients created by solute absorption

explanation: Water loves to follow the crowd! As the gut pumps in salts and sugars, water naturally flows right along with them through osmosis. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T7#GNS121_U1_T7_h5)

question: Which genetic combination is most commonly found in biological males?

options.A: One Y chromosome only
options.B: Two X chromosomes
options.C: One X and one Y chromosome
options.D: Three X chromosomes

explanation: Great job! Biological males usually inherit an X chromosome from the mother and a Y chromosome from the father, giving an XY pairing. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T2#GNS312_U4_T2_h1)

question: What is a major, life-threatening danger of an intracardiac injection?

options.A: Severe chronic kidney failure within two hours
options.B: Cardiac tamponade from bleeding into the pericardial sac
options.C: Total loss of vision in both eyes
options.D: Permanent yellow discoloration of the skin

explanation: Spot on. If blood leaks from the needle hole into the tight sac around the heart, it squeezes the heart so hard it can't beat anymore. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T14#GNS125_U3_T14_h6)

question: What is the main reason doctors taper corticosteroid therapy down gradually instead of stopping it overnight?

options.A: To prevent the development of severe allergic skin rashes
options.B: To keep blood sugar levels artificially low during withdrawal
options.C: To allow the adrenal glands time to resume natural cortisol production
options.D: To ensure the original disease symptoms never return again

explanation: A slow taper gives the sleeping adrenal glands a gentle wakeup call so they can remember how to make their own cortisol again safely. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T4#GNS223_U7_T4_h8)

question: Which emotional challenge is commonly experienced by family caregivers of patients with degenerative disorders?

options.A: Complete immunity to daily stress
options.B: Caregiver burnout and exhaustion
options.C: Instant recovery of physical strength
options.D: Sudden loss of all personal memories

explanation: Providing round-the-clock care for a progressively worsening condition can heavily drain family members, making caregiver support a vital part of nursing. You're learning fast! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h7)

question: What actually happens during the peer-review process before a study gets published in a journal?

options.A: The government checking the document for tax and financial compliance
options.B: Independent experts in the same field scrutinizing the manuscript for quality
options.C: The journal editor publishing the manuscript without any changes
options.D: Patients voting on whether they liked the treatment described

explanation: You got it! Other experts in the field carefully review the paper to make sure the science is solid before the public reads it. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T6#GNS217_U3_T6_h5)

question: A newborn delivered after a prolonged labor with severe cephalopelvic disproportion is at the highest risk for which condition?

options.A: Primary pulmonary hypertension
options.B: Neural tube closure failure
options.C: Congenital heart defect
options.D: Foetal skull injury

explanation: Prolonged pressure against a tight pelvis creates intense mechanical stress, making the infant very vulnerable to cranial trauma. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T16#GNS121_U6_T16_h2)

question: What is the best position for a patient during a thoracocentesis?

options.A: Lying flat on their stomach with the head turned to the side
options.B: Lying flat on their back with arms straight down
options.C: Sitting upright and leaning forward over a bedside table
options.D: Standing upright against a rigid wall with eyes closed

explanation: This posture widens the spaces between the ribs, making it safer and easier to insert the needle. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T17#GNS221_U2_T17_h3)

question: Why do standard antibiotics fail to cure viral infections like the common cold?

options.A: Antibiotics are destroyed by stomach acid before reaching viral cells
options.B: Viruses mutate too quickly for white blood cells to recognize them
options.C: Viruses hide inside healthy red blood cells away from medicines
options.D: Viruses do not possess the cellular structures that antibiotics target

explanation: Remember, antibiotics attack bacterial walls or parts that viruses simply don't have. That's why taking antibiotics for a viral flu won't help! [learn more](GST114_U3_T2#GST114_U3_T2_h1)

question: What happens inside the body during disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC)?

options.A: Widespread clotting exhausts platelets and factors, causing severe bleeding.
options.B: The body rapidly produces too many red blood cells.
options.C: Vitamin K is completely destroyed in the stomach.
options.D: Platelets permanently lose their ability to stick together.

explanation: DIC is a wild rollercoaster: the body forms tiny clots everywhere all at once, using up all its platelets and clotting factors. Once they are gone, the patient unfortunately starts bleeding heavily elsewhere. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T10#GNS311_U2_T10_h4)

question: Which of the following is a major objective of the Mother-Baby Package?

options.A: To reduce maternal, fetal, and newborn mortality rates
options.B: To increase the cost of maternity drugs in local clinics
options.C: To eliminate all traditional birth attendants completely
options.D: To transfer all pregnant women to tertiary teaching hospitals

explanation: Exactly right! Every clinical guideline and care package ultimately aims to keep both mum and baby safe, healthy, and alive. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h2)

question: What decides how thick or watery a colostomy stool will be?

options.A: The anatomical location of the stoma along the large intestine
options.B: The amount of physical exercise the patient does every day
options.C: The time of day the patient eats their main meal
options.D: The exact brand of the appliance pouch the patient wears

explanation: Exactly! Stool gets thicker the longer it travels through the colon because more water is absorbed along the way. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T14#GNS212_U1_T14_h2)

question: Which health promotion practice is most important for early detection of testicular cancer in young adult males?

options.A: Routine annual prostate-specific antigen tests
options.B: Frequent testing of post-void residual urine
options.C: Daily measurement of scrotal circumference
options.D: Regular testicular self-examination

explanation: Testicular self-examination empowers young men to notice hard lumps or changes early, when treatment is most successful. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h8)

question: Which nursing activity is vital for long-term cancer survivors?

options.A: Administering initial chemotherapy cycles in the acute ward
options.B: Performing major reconstructive surgeries in the clinic
options.C: Prescribing high-dose narcotic pain medications
options.D: Monitoring for late-appearing side effects of treatment

explanation: Even years later, survivors can develop delayed side effects affecting their heart or lungs, making watchful nursing care essential. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T11#GNS321_U1_T11_h9)

question: What is the safest sleeping position to teach parents to prevent SIDS (cot death)?

options.A: On the back (supine position)
options.B: On the stomach (prone position)
options.C: On either side with rolled towels
options.D: Upright in a soft infant seat

explanation: Always back to sleep! Placing babies flat on their backs for naps and bedtime is the safest way to keep their airways clear and lower the risk of SIDS. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T014#GNS226_U3_T014_h7)

question: How do grief and mourning differ from each other?

options.A: Grief is a medical diagnosis, while mourning is a nursing intervention
options.B: Grief only happens in hospitals, while mourning happens at home
options.C: Grief is the internal emotional feeling, while mourning is the outward expression
options.D: Grief lasts for years, while mourning ends after a few days

explanation: Think of grief as what happens inside your heart and mind, while mourning is how you show it on the outside through cultural or religious practices. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T10#GNS321_U4_T10_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of the feedback loop in the HPO (hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian) axis?

options.A: To regulate and coordinate hormone production between the brain and ovaries
options.B: To direct all excess hormones straight to the kidneys for filtration
options.C: To permanently shut down hormone release after puberty begins
options.D: To convert testosterone directly into adrenal adrenaline

explanation: Think of the feedback loop as a communication channel. The brain and ovaries talk back and forth to keep hormone levels balanced month after month. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T6#GNS121_U5_T6_h5)

question: When would a nurse researcher decide to use a quantitative design?

options.A: When writing a narrative history of nursing education
options.B: When measuring the exact change in blood glucose levels
options.C: When exploring the deep emotional meaning of grief
options.D: When observing unspoken cultural rituals in a community

explanation: Awesome! Because blood glucose can be counted and measured in numbers, it's a perfect fit for a quantitative study. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T3#GNS224_U1_T3_h2)

question: What are the three core action steps of Psychological First Aid?

options.A: Diagnose, Treat, Refer
options.B: Analyze, Process, Cure
options.C: Look, Listen, Link
options.D: Sedate, Calm, Rest

explanation: The three basic action principles of PFA guide helpers to observe safety, listen to needs, and connect people to resources. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h6)

question: The place where a microorganism normally lives and multiplies is called what?

options.A: A susceptible host
options.B: A reservoir
options.C: A portal of entry
options.D: A transmission route

explanation: A reservoir provides a safe home for pathogens to survive and multiply before finding a new host. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h2)

question: What is entomology?

options.A: The study of parasitic worms and flukes
options.B: The analysis of fungal infections
options.C: The scientific study of insects
options.D: The clinical study of human blood cells

explanation: Entomology is specifically the branch of zoology that focuses on insects and their relationship with the environment and humans. [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h1)

question: Why must drugs chosen for the formulary stay stable in tropical climates?

options.A: To make the drug containers look attractive on hospital shelves
options.B: To ensure the tablets dissolve instantly when dropped in cold water
options.C: To prevent the medicine from degrading rapidly under local weather conditions
options.D: to guarantee the medication smells pleasant during administration

explanation: Nigeria's warm weather can break down chemicals quickly. Drugs must be tough enough to hold their strength in our local climate! [learn more](GNS215_U1_T5#GNS215_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is the name of the delicate strip of skin on the underside of the penis that connects to the foreskin?

options.A: Corona
options.B: Preputial sac
options.C: Frenulum
options.D: Dorsal vein

explanation: Spot on! The frenulum is that sensitive little band of tissue underneath the penis. Surgeons take great care here because it has a rich blood supply. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T5#GNS311_U4_T5_h2)

question: How do drugs like praziquantel help clear out schistosomes and tapeworms?

options.A: Causing muscle paralysis by altering calcium ion permeability
options.B: Triggering an immediate rupture of the parasite reproductive organs
options.C: Dissolving the protective outer cuticle using strong digestive acids
options.D: Blocking the absorption of iron to starve adult worms of oxygen

explanation: Praziquantel causes calcium to rush into the worm, leading to strong muscle spasms and paralysis so it loses its grip on the host. [learn more](GST114_U3_T6#GST114_U3_T6_h7)

question: A client expresses fear that a contraceptive injection will cause permanent infertility based on rumors heard in the market. How should the nurse respond?

options.A: Provide accurate, gentle education and explain how the method temporarily works
options.B: Agree with the rumor to prevent any future arguments
options.C: Refuse to provide any family planning services to this client
options.D: Scold the client for listening to uneducated people in the community

explanation: Nurses must address fears and correct misconceptions with patience and clear scientific facts rather than judgment. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h6)

question: Which technology helps link patient prescriptions directly with pharmacy dispensing software?

options.A: Manual paper ledgers stored in wooden cabinets
options.B: Electronic health records and barcoding systems
options.C: Standard telephone landlines on the ward
options.D: Traditional wall clocks placed in the hallway

explanation: Digital records and barcode scanners speed up order transmission and reduce transcription mistakes between departments. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h8)

question: Why is a literature review so important when writing a proposal?

options.A: To criticize every nurse who worked before you
options.B: To fill up empty pages in the research document
options.C: To identify existing knowledge gaps on the topic
options.D: To gather personal opinions from hospital patients

explanation: Reviewing past studies shows you what has already been done and helps you find out what is still missing so your study adds real value. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T1#GNS224_U3_T1_h5)

question: At what point should health care waste be segregated?

options.A: After the cleaning staff transport it outside
options.B: At the exact point and time of generation
options.C: Only when the waste bins are completely full
options.D: During the final incineration process

explanation: Segregation must happen immediately where the waste is produced to prevent mixing hazardous and non-hazardous materials. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h3)

question: Which part of the chain of infection do standard precautions target the most?

options.A: The mode of transmission

options.C: The microbial reservoir
options.D: The infectious agent itself

question: What is the main force that pushes the baby down during the first stage of labour?

options.A: Voluntary maternal abdominal pushing
options.B: Intermittent uterine contractions
options.C: Gravity pulling the fetus downward
options.D: Manual traction by the midwife

question: Which placental hormone creates mild insulin resistance in the mother to guarantee a steady glucose supply for the baby?

options.A: Prolactin
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Human placental lactogen
options.D: Human chorionic gonadotropin

explanation: Human placental lactogen (hPL) cleverly saves more glucose in the mother's bloodstream so it's readily available to cross over and nourish the fetus. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T5#GNS121_U6_T5_h6)

question: Why do bacterial toxins in the gut cause diarrhea?

options.A: They block the reabsorption of solid waste in the rectum
options.B: They stimulate excess fluid secretion into the bowel lumen
options.C: They cause permanent paralysis of the abdominal muscles
options.D: They completely stop the production of digestive enzymes

explanation: When toxins irritate your gut lining, it reacts by rushing a lot of water and salt out into your intestines, causing watery stool to flush the germs out. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h3)

question: Which common bacterium causes most uncomplicated urinary tract infections?

options.A: Streptococcus pyogenes
options.B: Enterococcus faecalis
options.C: Escherichia coli
options.D: Pseudomonas aeruginosa

explanation: E. coli lives happily in our bowels, but when it enters the urinary tract, it becomes the number one culprit behind everyday UTIs! [learn more](GNS223_U8_T2#GNS223_U8_T2_h2)

question: Why do many women hide complications from an unsafe abortion in communities where it is heavily looked down upon?

options.A: Instructions given routinely by hospital doctors
options.B: Desire to test their own physical endurance
options.C: Fear of public judgment, disgrace, and legal trouble
options.D: Lack of pain receptors in the reproductive organs

explanation: Spot on. Stigma creates a scary wall of silence, making patients hide emergencies out of fear of being shamed or punished. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h3)

question: Which part of the female reproductive system is mainly affected in endometritis?

options.A: The inner lining of the uterus

options.C: The outer covering of the ovaries
options.D: The muscular wall of the womb

explanation: You've got this! 'Endo' means inside, and 'metritis' relates to the uterus. So endometritis is simply an infection or inflammation of the inner lining of the womb (the endometrium). [learn more](GNS216_U5_T20#GNS216_U5_T20_h1)

question: Why is the Trait theory considered a bit limited in modern nursing?

options.A: It requires every nurse to have advanced surgical training
options.B: It focuses too much on patient vital signs instead of administration
options.C: It ignores how leadership skills can be learned and shaped by situations
options.D: It proves that nurses never make good ward managers

explanation: While personal traits matter, Trait theory forgets that anyone can learn leadership skills and adapt to different situations on the ward. [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h2)

question: Through which main ways can toxic substances enter the human body?

options.C: Ingestion, inhalation, dermal absorption, and injection
options.D: Circulation, respiration, digestion, and excretion

question: What is the main goal of public health surveillance for nurses?

options.A: To manufacture vaccines in community health clinics
options.B: To punish hospitals that fail to report patient admissions
options.C: To prescribe antibiotics without a doctor's order
options.D: To systematically collect and analyze health data for disease trends

explanation: Surveillance keeps a close eye on disease patterns so we can catch outbreaks early and track down where germs are hiding. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h7)

question: How does an uncomplicated intestinal tapeworm infection usually present clinically?

options.A: It leads to rapid weight gain due to malabsorption of fats.
options.B: It always causes sudden high fevers and debilitating muscle paralysis.
options.C: It causes immediate respiratory failure by blocking the trachea.
options.D: It is frequently asymptomatic or causes only mild, non-specific digestive upset.

explanation: Well reasoned! Many people don't even know they have a tapeworm, or they might just feel slight tummy discomfort aside from seeing segments. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T24#GNS313_U2_T24_h4)

question: What is one of the best everyday ways to teach patients to lower their risk of catching STIs?

options.A: Underlining the importance of monthly pelvic ultrasound scans
options.B: Taking daily prophylactic doses of strong broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.C: Avoiding all physical contact with family members in public settings
options.D: Consistent and correct use of barrier methods like condoms

question: What is the main purpose of a survivorship care plan?

options.A: To manage acute surgical complications in the hospital
options.B: To replace the need for any further primary care visits
options.C: To guarantee that cancer will never return in the future
options.D: To outline treatment history and schedule ongoing surveillance

explanation: Think of it as a roadmap. A survivorship plan summarizes past treatments and maps out future health check-ups. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T11#GNS321_U1_T11_h9)

question: Which group is usually most affected by poor geographical access to health facilities?

options.A: Urban residents with private vehicles
options.B: Staff members working inside federal hospitals
options.C: Civil servants living near capital cities
options.D: Nomadic pastoralist communities

explanation: You nailed it! Nomadic and remote populations move often or live far from fixed clinics, making healthcare access quite tough. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T69#GNS214_U1_T69_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a helpful approach when communicating in a culturally diverse community?

options.A: Insulting local traditional practices to force quick compliance
options.B: Showing respect for community elders and family decision-makers
options.C: Learning basic greetings in the local language of the community
options.D: Being aware of cultural gender norms during consultations

explanation: Insulting cultural beliefs alienates patients and destroys trust, making them less likely to seek help at the clinic. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T12#GNS124_U5_T12_h5)

question: What kind of data do you mainly collect in qualitative research?

options.A: Words, text, and descriptions of human experiences
options.B: Statistical percentages of patient readmissions
options.C: Exact laboratory blood chemistry measurements
options.D: Precise numerical vital signs recorded hourly

explanation: While quantitative loves numbers, qualitative loves words! It looks at interview notes and stories to understand human experiences. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T6#GNS224_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is the main difference between monitoring and evaluation in a BCC program?

options.A: Monitoring is done only by doctors, while evaluation is done by patients
options.B: Evaluation happens before the project starts, and monitoring never happens
options.C: There is no difference; both words mean exactly the same thing
options.D: Monitoring is ongoing during the project, while evaluation measures final impact

explanation: Think of monitoring as checking your progress while running the race, and evaluation as looking at your overall performance and medals when the race is finished. You've got this distinction down! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h8)

question: Why is it important to have a clear 'case definition' when investigating a disease outbreak?

options.A: It eliminates the need for environmental sanitation and vector control.
options.B: It stops the infectious agent from mutating into a stronger strain.
options.C: It ensures all investigators look for the exact same symptoms when counting cases.
options.D: It automatically cures patients once they meet the official criteria.

explanation: Spot on! A clear case definition means every health worker is using the same checklist, so everyone accurately counts and tracks the right cases. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h6)

question: Why do old family arguments often resurface when a relative enters the terminal phase of illness?

options.A: Family members try to impress the medical staff
options.B: Hospital policies require families to argue before visiting
options.C: Medications given to the patient cause hallucinations in visitors
options.D: The approaching loss heightens emotional stress and tension

explanation: The impending death of a loved one puts intense psychological pressure on family relationships, unearthing past conflicts. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h4)

question: What do we call the mild mood swings and crying spells many women feel in the first week after birth?

options.A: Baby blues
options.B: Puerperal fever
options.C: Major depressive disorder
options.D: Postpartum psychosis

explanation: Spot on! The 'baby blues' are very common and normal due to sudden hormone shifts. They usually pass on their own within two weeks with a little love and support. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T013#GNS226_U3_T013_h6)

question: Which type of budget covers long-term investments and big purchases like a new X-ray machine?

options.A: Personnel budget
options.B: Cash flow budget
options.C: Capital budget
options.D: Operating budget

explanation: Capital budgets are for the big-ticket items—like heavy machinery and building upgrades—that stay with the hospital for many years. [learn more](GST321_U1_T24#GST321_U1_T24_h2)

question: Why must a nurse line up the pressure monitor with the phlebostatic axis before reading blood pressure numbers?

options.C: To make sure the blood sample does not get contaminated
options.D: To stop the arterial line from forming a blood clot

question: A hospitalized patient has a very low prealbumin level and a very high C-reactive protein (CRP). How should you read these results?

options.A: The low prealbumin is likely caused by inflammation rather than pure starvation.
options.B: The lab results cancel each other out and provide no useful clinical data.
options.C: The high CRP proves the patient is absorbing all dietary proteins properly.
options.D: The patient definitely needs an emergency tube feeding for protein deficiency.

explanation: Spotting inflammation (via high CRP) helps you realize that low protein levels might be due to the illness itself, not just poor eating. Clinical puzzle solved! [learn more](GNS227_U5_T005#GNS227_U5_T005_h5)

question: What does an autoclave primarily use to sterilize infectious medical waste?

options.A: High-pressure steam
options.B: Dry freezing air

question: Which nutrients are most easily lost when vegetables are boiled in a lot of water and the water is thrown away?

question: Why do cooks love adding waterleaf to traditional Nigerian soups and stews?

question: How can a nurse manager protect their decision-making process from personal mental biases?

question: Why are nurses considered the heartbeat of safe hospital waste management?

question: Why is studying insects (entomology) so important for nurses and healthcare workers?

question: What is the main goal of medications used for degenerative neurological disorders?

question: Why do antigen-presenting cells need to display pieces of a germ on MHC molecules?

question: Why does stopping your antibiotics halfway through a course cause drug resistance?

question: A patient shares that her husband constantly insults her, threatens to chase her out, and cuts her off from her family. What kind of abuse is this?

question: When should a nurse put on a disposable gown and gloves for contact precautions?

question: What is a major consequence when clients bypass primary facilities to visit tertiary psychiatric hospitals directly?

question: When should the nurse wash their hands during a home visit bag procedure?

question: What is the number one direct cause of maternal death all over the world?

question: A nurse notices more children losing weight in the months right before the new harvest. What activity helped spot this trend?

question: Why is involving local community members in school health campaigns advantageous?

question: Where are parasympathetic terminal ganglia typically located?

question: What type of data is mostly used in explanatory research designs?

question: What is the main purpose of a safety box in a clinical injection setting?

question: What is a major physical benefit of early ambulation on the respiratory system?

question: What is the best way to handle a patient who is extremely anxious about minor symptoms?

options.C: It is a mild response that always goes away without any treatment.
options.D: It is completely unpredictable and does not depend on the drug dose.

explanation: Think of an idiosyncratic reaction as a surprise response! Unlike normal side effects that we expect, these happen out of nowhere due to a patient's unique body makeup, not because of a high dose. You've got this! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T9#GNS125_U5_T9_h1)

question: What is the most common local side effect of a topical skin medication?

options.A: Sudden kidney failure
options.B: Contact dermatitis and redness at the site
options.C: Complete hair loss on the scalp
options.D: Severe high blood pressure

explanation: Mild skin irritation, redness, or itching right where the cream was applied are the most common reactions to topical products. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T12#GNS215_U6_T12_h8)

question: What is a major effect of malnutrition in school children?

options.A: Impaired learning capacity and weakened immunity
options.B: Enhanced resistance to common viral infections
options.C: Rapid acceleration in physical height and bone density
options.D: Increased ability to focus for long hours

explanation: That's right! Without proper nutrients, the body and brain struggle, leading to poor concentration, tiredness, and frequent sickness. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h5)

question: What is the very first thing you should do before preparing to measure a medication?

options.A: Shake the empty measuring cup vigorously
options.B: Pour the medication directly down the drain
options.C: Heat the glass bottle in a microwave oven
options.D: Perform hand hygiene and put on gloves

explanation: Safety first! Standard infection control always starts with clean hands before touching any patient supplies or medications. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T21#GNS122_U1_T21_h4)

question: Why must a nurse wear PPE when performing last offices?

options.A: To protect against exposure to infectious body fluids
options.B: To comply with fire safety rules in the hospital
options.C: To prevent the family from recognizing the nurse later
options.D: To keep the nurse's uniform from getting wrinkled

explanation: Pathogens can still be present in bodily fluids after death, making standard precautions and PPE essential for staff safety. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h3)

question: A patient asks why the doctor adjusts their tiopronin dose using 24-hour urine collections. What is your best nursing response?

options.A: To find the exact dose that lowers your urine cystine enough to stop stones from forming
options.B: To check if your liver is completely immune to protein toxicity
options.C: To measure how much calcium your bones are losing while taking the drug
options.D: To ensure you are drinking the exact recommended liters of soda daily

explanation: We use 24-hour urine tests to find the sweet spot: enough medicine to keep cystine levels low and prevent stones, without taking more than necessary. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T4#GNS223_U8_T4_h4)

question: How does long-term intestinal schistosomiasis end up causing portal hypertension?

options.A: Adult worms multiply rapidly inside the heart and increase overall blood pressure.
options.B: Intestinal bleeding drains blood volume, forcing the heart to pump at a dangerous rate.
options.C: The kidneys fail to filter salt, causing fluid overload throughout the entire body.
options.D: Trapped eggs cause liver fibrosis that blocks blood flow through the portal vein system.

explanation: When eggs get trapped in the liver, the body forms scar tissue (fibrosis). This traffic jam blocks normal blood flow, raising pressure in the portal vein. Pathophysiology made clear! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T10#GNS214_U1_T10_h7)

question: Why must nurses remind patients never to stop taking their antidepressants all of a sudden?

options.A: Abrupt discontinuation instantly cures the chemical imbalance
options.B: Stopping quickly causes immediate permanent brain damage
options.C: Sudden cessation can trigger withdrawal symptoms and a return of depression
options.D: Patients will develop a physical addiction to the medication

explanation: Spot on! Stopping suddenly can cause uncomfortable withdrawal effects and bring the depression rushing back. Medication always needs to be tapered off safely under medical guidance. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T2#GNS324_U4_T2_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a form of social stigma for persons with physical disabilities?

options.A: Receiving appropriate medical rehabilitation therapies
options.B: Encountering buildings with no wheelchair ramps
options.C: Being excluded from community social gatherings
options.D: Facing derogatory language and public staring

explanation: Spot on! Rehab therapy is supportive healthcare. Staring, lack of ramps, and exclusion are unfair barriers and forms of stigma. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T14#GNS225_U5_T14_h5)

question: What is the key sign of a post-dural puncture headache?

options.A: It gets worse when the patient sits up and improves when lying flat
options.B: It feels like a sharp electrical shock running down both legs
options.C: It stays at the exact same intensity regardless of body position
options.D: It only occurs during the night and disappears by afternoon

explanation: You nailed it! Low fluid pressure pulls on pain-sensitive areas when upright, which eases up when the patient lies horizontal. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h7)

question: An IV bag of 1,000 mL Normal Saline is ordered to run over 8 hours using a pump. What is the hourly rate?

options.A: 150 mL/hr
options.B: 80 mL/hr
options.C: 125 mL/hr
options.D: 100 mL/hr

explanation: Divide total volume by total hours: 1,000 mL ÷ 8 hours = 125 mL/hr. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T23#GNS122_U1_T23_h8)

question: What naturally happens to kidney filtration (GFR) during a normal pregnancy?

options.A: It stops entirely in the third trimester
options.B: It remains completely unchanged
options.C: It increases significantly
options.D: It decreases by half

explanation: You've got this! Because a pregnant body carries extra blood volume, the kidneys have to work harder and filter faster, raising the GFR by up to fifty percent. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T007#GNS226_U4_T007_h1)

question: Which combination of symptoms is a major red flag for a postpartum uterine infection?

options.A: Mild swelling in both ankles
options.B: Foul-smelling lochia and fever
options.C: Gradual lightening of lochia color
options.D: Increased appetite and energy

explanation: Spot on! Fever combined with lower tummy pain and bad-smelling lochia are classic signs that the uterus might be infected and needs medical attention. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T021#GNS226_U3_T021_h6)

question: Why do health programs often fail if nurses ignore local cultural values?

options.A: Because government laws forbid treating people with different beliefs
options.B: Because the community feels disrespected and rejects outside interference
options.C: Because local leaders charge heavy fines for unapproved advice
options.D: Because medications lose their chemical potency in different cultures

explanation: Always respect local culture! When people feel understood and respected, they are much more likely to welcome healthcare programs. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T3#GNS225_U1_T3_h4)
